rows.note: Use 牌子 as the all-purpose choice when “make” means a product brand or make.

example.english: Do you know what make this phone is?
example.traditional: 你知唔知呢部電話係咩牌子？
example.jyutping: nei5 zi1 m4 zi1 ni1 bou6 din6 waa2 hai6 me1 paai4 zi2

rows.note: Use 生產商 for the manufacturer or company that made the product, rather than its brand.

example.english: The make of this camera is a Japanese company.
example.traditional: 呢部相機嘅生產商係間日本公司。
example.jyutping: ni1 bou6 soeng1 gei1 ge3 sang1 caan2 soeng1 hai6 gaan1 jat6 bun2 gung1 si1

rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for making, creating, cooking, or putting together something such as a plan.

example.jyutping: ngo5 mui5 jat6 dou1 zing2 daan6 gou1

rows.note: Use this when an action or situation causes someone or something to end up in a state or causes a result, including making someone cry.

example.english: You make me unable to sleep with all that noise.
example.jyutping: nei5 gam3 cou4 gaau2 dou3 ngo5 fan3 m4 zoek6

rows.note: Use 款式 when “make” refers to the style or overall form of an object.

example.english: I really like the make of this chair; it looks sturdy.
example.traditional: 我幾鍾意呢張櫈嘅款式，睇落好實淨。
example.jyutping: ngo5 gei2 zung1 ji3 ni1 zoeng1 dang3 ge3 fun2 sik1 tai2 lok6 hou2 sat6 zing6

rows.note: Use this specifically for making or earning money or profit, rather than making points or gaining status.

example.english: I go to work just to make money.
example.jyutping: ngo5 faan1 gung1 zau6 hai6 wai6 zo2 wan2 cin2

rows.note: Use this for arithmetic or other statements that one quantity adds up to or amounts to another.

example.english: Three plus two make a total of five.
example.jyutping: saam1 gaa1 ji6 dang2 jyu1 ng5
